title: What's New — Cleaner Layout + Live Stability Fixes
summary: PulseGuard v0.6.3 reorganizes implementation files under Runtime while preserving automatic update compatibility from v0.6.2, and it hardens the live 3-minute stability experience so the UI publishes PREPARING/RUNNING evidence immediately, video playback cannot PASS from UI FPS alone when decoder/media progress is unproven, and the speaker check uses a cleaner stereo chime.

items.heading: One obvious launcher
items.detail: Customers launch PulseGuard PC.vbs. Internal engines, rules, assets, the driver catalog, updater, diagnostics modules and third-party notices live under Runtime.

items.heading: Safe v0.6.2 migration bridge
items.detail: The v0.6.3 release temporarily carries the exact legacy paths required by the already-shipped v0.6.2 updater. Cleanup does not run until the complete Runtime payload has been verified.

items.heading: Customer state stays outside Runtime
items.detail: Data, Logs, Reports and Backups remain at the install root and are preserved across updates. An existing Rules\system_profile.json is migrated into Runtime\Rules before the legacy Rules directory can be removed.

items.heading: Shortcut compatibility preserved
items.detail: Legacy main/start/VBS/CMD entry points become small Runtime relays and are hidden after successful migration rather than deleted, so existing shortcuts and scheduled entry points continue to work.

items.heading: Evidence and diagnostics retained
items.detail: All v0.6.2 Evidence & Accuracy diagnostics remain included: repair verification still uses explicit states such as UNVERIFIED when proof is insufficient, WHEA evidence remains scoped to the exact stability-test window, driver provenance remains recorded, unsupported VRAM integrity remains N/A, and PulseGuard still does not claim LatencyMon-style driver-level attribution without equivalent evidence.

items.heading: Visible video / motion proof
items.detail: The video test now includes a visible motion scene and tracks decoder/media progress separately from WPF presentation FPS. A stalled or otherwise unproven decoder can no longer receive PASS merely because the WPF window itself renders at about 60 FPS; a visible PulseGuard motion scene keeps the test window obviously active even when the media surface is black.

items.heading: Live test starts visibly
items.detail: The stability worker publishes PREPARING status before evidence setup and RUNNING status as soon as active CPU/RAM/disk/graphics load begins. First-run sensor-provider acquisition is time-bounded and timed temperature samples do not start new downloads.

items.heading: Cleaner stereo chime
items.detail: The old repeated synthetic tone sequence is replaced with a softer stereo chime that identifies the left channel, right channel, then both channels, and it repeats only once during the three-minute run instead of every 30 seconds.
